checklist.label: Plan name and the COBRA administrator's name, address and telephone number
Qualified beneficiaries, by status or name, and the date coverage ends
Each qualified beneficiary's independent right to elect
How to elect, the election period, and the date by which to elect
What happens if you do not elect or you waive, and how to revoke a waiver
The coverage offered and when it begins
The maximum coverage period, the end date, and early termination
Extensions for disability or a second qualifying event
Your duty to give notice of a second qualifying event or a disability determination
The amount each qualified beneficiary must pay
Payment due dates, monthly payment, grace periods, where to pay, and late payment
Keeping the administrator informed of current addresses
A statement that the notice does not fully describe coverage, and where to find more

readiness.label: Stated dates and terms meet the minimums
No personal identifiers in the draft

findings.message: For termination or reduction of hours the maximum period is 18 months, and the notice does not state 18 months.
The election deadline stated in the notice is earlier than 60 days after the later of the loss of coverage and the notice date.
The notice requires the first payment sooner than 45 days after the election.
The notice gives a grace period shorter than 30 days.
The notice states a premium above 102 percent of the plan cost (150 percent is allowed only during a disability extension).
The notice goes out after the election notice deadline.
No mailing address for the COBRA administrator was found.
The notice does not name the party responsible for administering COBRA coverage.
The notice does not identify the qualified beneficiaries who may elect.
The notice does not say that each qualified beneficiary has an independent right to elect.
The notice does not state the election period (at least 60 days).
The notice does not describe how to revoke a waiver before the election deadline.
The notice does not explain what can end continuation coverage early.
The notice does not describe the disability extension.
The notice does not describe the extension for a second qualifying event.
The notice does not explain the duty to report that a disabled beneficiary is no longer disabled.
The notice does not describe the notice to give after a Social Security disability determination.
The notice does not give the time limit for notifying the plan of a disability determination or a second qualifying event.
The notice does not give the address to which payments should be sent.
The notice does not explain the consequences of late payment or non-payment.
The notice does not explain the importance of keeping the administrator informed of current addresses.
The notice does not state that it does not fully describe continuation coverage and where more complete information is available.
The notice does not say that a parent or legal guardian may elect for a minor child.
The notice does not say that the employee or spouse may elect on behalf of the other qualified beneficiaries.
The notice does not mention the effect on other coverage rights, such as special enrollment.
The notice does not say when continuation coverage begins.
The notice does not explain how COBRA and Medicare interact, as the DOL model election notice does.

notChecked: Whether the wording is legally sufficient in context. A pattern can find that an item is addressed, not that it is right.
Whether the premium amounts, plan details and beneficiaries named are correct for your plan.
Whether the notice was actually delivered, and how (first-class mail, separate notices to a spouse at another address).
State continuation (mini-COBRA) laws, and plans of employers with fewer than 20 employees, which federal COBRA does not cover.
The notice of unavailability, the notice of early termination and the employer notice to the administrator.
